Classify a pedon under the Comprehensive Soil Classification System of Japan

Source: R/key-cscj2011.R
classify_cscj2011.Rd

Keys a PedonRecord through the Comprehensive Soil Classification System of Japan, First Approximation (Obara et al. 2011), following its key to great groups. Experimental: this release keys the ten great groups (Man-made soils, Organic soils, Podzols, Andosols, Dark Red soils, Lowland soils, Red-Yellow soils, Stagnic soils, Brown Forest soils, Regosols), their 27 groups (for instance Fulvic and Allophanic Andosols, Calcaric Dark Red soils, Brown Lowland soils) and their 116 subgroups (Haplic, Argic, Low-humic, Terrace ...) and their 381 soil series groups (lithic, skeletal, fine-textured, high-humic ..., read with the new attributes texture_class_jp and hardness_yamanaka_mm), and gives the soil phases of chapter VIII (temperature, estimated from the air temperature plus 2 C when the soil temperature is not recorded, and the man-made phases). Each level gives the English name of the text's appendix 2 and, in levels$name_native, the Japanese one.

Usage

classify_cscj2011(
  pedon,
  rules = NULL,
  on_missing = c("warn", "silent", "error"),
  gapfill = FALSE
)

Arguments

pedon

A PedonRecord.

rules

Optional pre-loaded rule set (load_rules("cscj2011")).

on_missing

One of "warn" (default), "silent", "error".

gapfill

Opt-in within-pedon gap-fill, as in classify_usda.

Value

A ClassificationResult with system_id "cscj2011", the deepest class in name, the great group in rsg_or_order, the classes of each level in levels (with name_native), the key trace, provisional_because (classes before the assigned one that could not be decided), and in phases the soil phases of chapter VIII (temperature and man-made phases; the class name is left as it is).

Details

The CSCJ shares most of its diagnostics with the Soil Classification System of Japan (2017), and soilKey reads them with the same code (see classify_scsj2017 for the attributes read), by the CSCJ's own limits where it has them: the argic horizon (the WRB 2006 clay increase), the immature kuroboku feature (P retention as its only substitute), and the dark red colour of the Dark Red soils, which also read the origin from limestone or calcareous deposits (rock_origin, layer_origin, the site parent_material, caco3_pct). The choices where the text is silent are listed in system.file("rules", "cscj2011", "readings.yaml", package = "soilKey").

References

Obara, H., Ohkura, T., Takata, Y., Kohyama, K., Maejima, Y. and Hamazaki, T. (2011). Comprehensive Soil Classification System of Japan, First Approximation. Bulletin of the National Institute for Agro-Environmental Sciences 29: 1-73.

See also

make_cscj2011_example, classify_scsj2017, soilkey_systems.

Examples

res <- classify_cscj2011(make_cscj2011_example("dark_red"), on_missing = "silent")
res$name
#> [1] "typic Argic Calcaric Dark Red soils"
res$levels
#>           level   code                                name
#> 1  great_groups      E                      Dark Red soils
#> 2        groups     E1             Calcaric Dark Red soils
#> 3     subgroups   E1AR       Argic Calcaric Dark Red soils
#> 4 series_groups E1ARTY typic Argic Calcaric Dark Red soils
#>                  name_native
#> 1               暗赤色土大群
#> 2             石灰性暗赤色土
#> 3     粘土集積石灰性暗赤色土
#> 4 典型粘土集積石灰性暗赤色土
